text:
maria: Heads-up — seeing ~20% p50 regression on the Qwen-8k route after runtime change in kernel selection. Attaching short perf dump and metric snippet.

deploy-bot: deploy finished: runtime-service@prod v3.14.2 (sha: a1b2c3) :rocket:

maria: perf summary (sampling over 10k requests):
```
model: qwen-8k
p50(before): 12.4ms  p50(after): 14.8ms  (+19%)
p95(before): 38.7ms p95(after): 44.1ms (+14%)
kv_cache_hit_rate(before): 87.2% -> 60.4%
kv_evictions/s: 4.1 -> 18.6
GPU mem usage: +400MB on avg
```

alex: Oof. Eviction/sec jump + memory increase points at either (a) KV layout change causing fragmentation, or (b) we fell back to a suboptimal kernel that doesn't use packed KV. Did you capture kernel selection logs?

maria: pasted the runtime router log excerpt — it shows a fallback to `generic_kv_copy` for many Qwen calls at 12:03:22. Also saw a handful of `quant_kv_accel` failures with "unsupported stride".

jin: That matches a precision-handling mismatch. FP8/quantized KV path expects tightly-packed stride and aligned head dims. If model or tokenizer split changed head alignments we could hit the fallback. Fallback -> extra mem copies -> eviction thrash.

alex: Quick experiment ideas:
- verify head_dim % 64 alignment and layout for the Qwen-8k build
- force kernel preference for `quant_kv_accel` on a canary to measure delta
- try reduced batch_delay to limit batch size and KV pressure for small interactive queries

sasha: I'll put a small config suggestion here to try on the canary:
```
# runtime per-model overrides
models:
  qwen-8k:
    kernel_policy: ["quant_kv_accel","fp16_kv_copy"]
    batcher:
      max_batch_delay_ms: 6   # was 12
      prefer_small_shapes: true
    kv_cache:
      eviction: segmented_mru
      prefix_protection: true
```

maria: started a canary with that config on a single dedicated pod (canary-qwen-1). Initial 1k requests: p50 -> 12.7ms, p95 -> 40.2ms, kv_hit_rate -> 82.1%, evictions/s -> 6.4. So p50 mostly recovered, overall hit rate much better. tail still slightly higher than pre-change.

jin: Nice. Tail still elevated likely due to two things: (1) quant_kv_accel has a longer cold-path on first usage (JIT/kernels selected), (2) batching heuristics create occasional large batches that trigger slow kernel variants. We should instrument per-request kernel selection + latency. perf-bot can add a histogram.

perf-bot: added metrics: `runtime.kernel.selection.latency_ms` and `runtime.kv.kernel_type.count` on the Qwen route. Data in grafana -> /d/runtime-kernels/qwen-kernels

alex: Long-term fixes: (a) Make kernel router aware of KV layout/alignment metadata — prefer quant path only when head_dim%packed_stride==0. (b) Add a lightweight preflight that verifies kernel readiness and warms quant kernels during the first N requests to avoid cold-path tail. (c) Add segmented_mru with prefix-protection as default for interactive routes to keep prompt prefixes pinned.

maria: Agreed. Also saw a small memory-alloc pattern in the profiler: repeated allocations of 256KB slabs during KV copy. That suggests our pooling isn't reusing quant buffers when falling back.

jin: Action items:
- alex: prototype kernel-router change to consult `model.metadata.head_alignment` and prefer `quant_kv_accel` only when aligned (owner: alex, ETA: EOD tomorrow)
- sasha: roll `batcher.max_batch_delay_ms: 6` to all Qwen-8k pods behind a canary flag (owner: sasha, ETA: today)
- maria: collect 100k requests with per-request kernel_type label and share p50/p95 (owner: maria, ETA: 2h)
- jin: add a microbenchmark showing FP8 quantized KV path vs fp16 copy memory/work per step (owner: jin, ETA: EOD)

sasha: scheduling a gradual canary rollout 5% -> 25% -> 100% if metrics stable (+auto-rollback on p95 > +10%).

maria: thanks — will watch the canary graphs. tagging @alex @jin for followups. :thumbsup:

alex: Also adding small config to train the kernel warmup: on new model/policy flip, run N=8 warmup calls with synthetic short seq to JIT kernels. Will post patch.

maria: patch landed on canary. After 10 warmup calls, tail normalized to ~+3% vs baseline. Looks promising. We'll keep canary running for a day before wider roll.

sasha: nice work. Adding notes to runbook about head-alignment checks when onboarding new builds/models.

maria: Closing loop once canary finishes. Thanks team.
